title: Recovery and Deep Sequencing of Short ssDNA Pools from Coacervate Droplets
author: Holtmannspötter, Machatzke, et al.
materials: NEBNext Ultra II Q5 Master Mix
Monarch Spin PCR & DNA Cleanup Kit
NucleoMag NGS Clean-up and Size Selection

First, we describe how to prepare fuel-dependent complex coacervates in the presence of an ssDNA library. Then, we explain how to separate the phases and recover the ssDNA for downstream analysis.1.Prepare complex coacervates and separate phases.a.Thaw ssDNA library (and tagged RNA, if used) on ice.b.Prepare complex coacervates mix (900 μL).ReagentStockFinalV/μLMES pH 5.3500 mM200 mM400RG3 peptide155 mM23 mM150polyU41 mM4.1 mM100N30 library3 μg/μL9 μg3Tagged RNA (optional)100 μM1 μM10ddH2O237 or 247Note: Adding tagged RNA makes the pellet easier to detect after centrifugation. While this is not strictly necessary, it is recommended for initial trials. The RNA sequence is not critical, as the RNase cocktail will remove all RNAs.c.Add 100 μL 400 mM EDC solution to the complex coacervates master mix. Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down.Note: Within seconds of mixing the sample with fuel, the solution should become visibly turbid, indicating coacervate formation. If this does not occur and the sample remains clear, refer to problem 1. For representative static images and time-lapse videos of the expected turbidity and droplet morphology, see Donau et al., 2020.2CRITICAL: From the addition of EDC until the supernatant is removed, it is crucial to adhere to all incubation times precisely and work quickly. The fuel-dependent system has a very short lifespan.d.Incubate for 1 minute at ∼25°C.e.Spin for 3 minutes at 16.000 g in a centrifuge set to 25°C.CRITICAL: The temperature should not exceed 30°C during centrifugation. The lifetime of droplets is greatly affected by temperature. Lower temperatures may greatly extend lifetimes, whereas higher temperatures can drastically decrease them.f.After centrifugation, immediately remove all supernatant very thoroughly and store it for downstream analysis.Note: Use a P1000 to remove most of the bulk of the supernatant without disturbing the pellet. Then, using a P10, remove as much liquid as possible from the pellet. Discard these small volumes.g.Resuspend the pellet in 10 μL 5 M NaCl by pipetting up and down.h.After resuspension, the solution should be clear. Add 40 μL ddH2O.i.Use the Monarch Spin PCR & DNA Cleanup Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions for the “small oligo” protocol to clean up 50 μL of pellet and 50 μL of supernatant:i.Add 100 μL Buffer BZ to the solution.ii.Add 300 μL Isopropanol. Mix well by pipetting up and down. Do not vortex.iii.Transfer 450 μL solution onto a spin column and spin for 1 minute at 16,000 g. Discard flow-through.iv.Add 500 μL Buffer WZ to the spin column and spin for 1 minute at 16,000 g. Discard flow-through.v.Repeat step iv.vi.Transfer the spin column to a fresh 1.5 mL sample tube. Spin empty for 1 minute at 16.000 g to remove residual buffer.vii.Transfer the spin column to a fresh sample tube. Add 10 μL ddH2O to the center of the matrix to elute DNA. Spin for 1 minute at 16,000 g, then discard the spin column.2.Digest polyU RNA from both samples.a.Add 1 μL RNase cocktail to both samples.Note: Always keep enzyme mixes in −20°C cooling blocks.b.Incubate the samples in a thermocycler for 2 hours at 37°C, followed by 10 minutes at 65°C with the lid set to 105°C.Note: 2 μL of the recovered, RNase-digested ssDNA can be used for analysis via urea-PAGE gel (20% 19:1 acrylamide: bisacrylamide). If low yields are observed in this step, refer to problem 2.

This step describes how to prepare ssDNA for sequencing using sequence-agnostic, orientation-specific splinted ligations. We then provide a brief overview of how to perform sequencing using an iSeq 100. However, any Illumina-type sequencer that is compatible with the adapters can be used. If you are proceeding with in-house sequencing, remember to thaw the sequencing reagents according to the manufacturer’s instructions. This process usually takes 9–18 hours.3.Ligation of isolated ssDNA to the adapter oligonucleotides via splinted ligation.a.Thaw adapter and splint oligos on ice.b.Prepare 10 μL of P5 adapter and splint mix per ssDNA sample.ReagentStockFinalV/μLT4 DNA Ligase reaction buffer10×1×1SRSLY P5 adapter100 μM10 μM1SRSLY P5 splint100 μM20 μM2ddH2O6c.Prepare 10 μL of P7 adapter and splint mix per ssDNA sample.ReagentStockFinalV/μLT4 DNA Ligase reaction buffer10×1×1SRSLY P7 adapter100 μM10 μM1SRSLY P7 splint100 μM20 μM2ddH2O6d.Anneal oligonucleotides by heating the reaction mix to 95°C for 10 seconds and then cooling them down to 10°C at a ramp rate of 0.1°C/s in a thermocycler.e.Prepare 78 μL Ligation mix per ssDNA sample. Mix well by pipetting up and down or vortexing.ReagentStockFinalV/μLT4 DNA Ligase reaction buffer10×1×8P5 adapter and splint mix9P7 adapter and splint mix9ssDNA sample9PEG-800050%20%32ddH2O11f.Add 1 μL (30 U) T4 DNA Ligase and 1 μL T4 PNK (10 U) to the reaction mix. Carefully mix by pipetting up and down.g.Incubate ∼16 hours at 25°C in a thermocycler with the lid set to “off”.h.Incubate 10 minutes at 65°C with the lid set to 105°C to inactivate proteins.i.Use the Monarch Spin PCR & DNA Cleanup Kit with the standard cleanup protocol to clean up 80 μL of each sample. Change the ratio of sample: binding buffer to 3:1:i.Add 240 μL Buffer BZ to the solution. Mix well by pipetting up and down. Do not vortex.ii.Transfer 320 μL solution onto a spin column and spin for 1 minute at 16,000 g. Discard flow-through.iii.Add 200 μL Buffer WZ to the spin column and spin for 1 minute at 16,000 g. Discard flow-through.iv.Repeat step iv.v.Transfer the spin column to a fresh 1.5 mL sample tube. Spin empty for 1 minute at 16.000 g to remove residual buffer.vi.Transfer the spin column to a fresh 1.5 mL sample tube. Add 17 μL ddH2O to the center of the matrix to elute DNA. Spin for 1 minute at 16,000 g, then discard the spin column.Note: 2 μL of the final cleaned-up product can be used for analysis via Urea-PAGE gel (20% 19:1 acrylamide: bisacrylamide) or a TapeStation or Bioanalyzer. The adapters in this work are 33 nt and 34 nt long, meaning the expected ligated product is library length + 67 nt, in the case of N30, 97 nt. If low yields are observed, refer to problem 3.Pause point: At this point, it is possible to store the samples at −20°C and continue the protocol at a later point.4.Addition of index- and sequencing-primers via PCR.a.Prepare the following PCR mix:ReagentStockFinalV/μLadapter ligated DNA15NEBNext Ultra II Q5 Master Mix2×1×25Index primer (NEB primer set)5Universal primer (NEB primer set)5b.Run the following PCR cycle:StepsTemperatureTimeCyclesInitial Denaturation98°C30 sec1Denaturation98°C10 sec15 cyclesAnnealing/Extension65°C75 secFinal extension65°C300 sec1Hold4°CforeverCRITICAL: Do not use the same index primer for multiple samples! Make a note of which index primer is used for each sample and the correct index read of that primer. You will need to provide this information to the sequencer.c.Clean up using NucleoMag NGS Clean-up and Size Selection:i.Vortex NucleoMag solution until all beads are resuspended.ii.Add 45 μL bead solution to the finished PCR reaction, and incubate for 5 minutes.iii.Put on a magnetic rack, incubate for 5 minutes, and remove the supernatant.iv.Add 200 μL 80% Ethanol while on the magnetic rack, incubate 30 seconds, and remove supernatant.v.Repeat step iv. Ensure that as much liquid as possible is removed.vi.Air dry beads for a maximum of 5 minutes.vii.Remove from the magnetic rack. Add 33 μL of 0.1 TE buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA), mix well by pipetting up and down to resuspend beads. Incubate 2 minutes.viii.Put on a magnetic rack, incubate 5 minutes.ix.Transfer 30 μL to a fresh 0.2 mL PCR tube.d.Confirm the success of the library preparation, e.g., using a TapeStation with a D1000 cassette if available.Pause point: At this point, it is possible to store the samples at −20°C and continue the protocol at a later point.5.Based on the TapeStation concentration measurements, dilute and mix your library for loading concentrations.Note: For calculations, use the peak corresponding to the correct library length (for the same adapters and library length, this peak is at 154 bp), the peak corresponding to an adapter dimer (for the same adapters, this peak is at 124 bp) and the peak corresponding to a double insert (for the same adapters and library length, this peak is at 184 bp). Add these three peaks together to calculate the total sample library concentration.a.In low-binding tubes, dilute each sample library to 1 nM with 10 mM Tris, pH 8.5.b.Mix 10 μL of each 1 nM sample library in a low-binding tube. This yields a 1 nM mixed sample library.c.Prepare the final loading library by preparing this last dilution step and adding in the PhiX Control Library:ReagentStockFinalV/μLmixed sample library1 nM50 pM5PhiX Control V31 nM50 pM5Tris pH 8.510 mM10 mM906.Prepare the iSeq 100 and sequencing cassette according to the manufacturer’s instructions:a.Load the sequencing cassette with the flow cell and library into the iSeq 100:i.Thaw the flow cell for 30 minutes at ∼25°C.ii.Unpack the thawed sequencing cassette.iii.Invert the sequencing cassette 5 times.iv.Tap the sequencing cassette on the table 5 times.v.Pierce foil protecting the library loading well with a pipette tip.vi.With a fresh pipette tip, load 20 μL of the final loading library into the library loading well.vii.Insert the flow cell into the sequencing cassette.viii.Insert the sequencing cassette into the iSeq 100.b.On the sequencer, set up a new run in Local Run Manager:i.Select “Generate FastQ” as the method.ii.Name your experiment.iii.Choose “Custom” as the library preparation protocol.iv.Choose 1 Index primer read (P7) with a read length of 6.v.Choose dual-read mode with a read length of 151 each.vi.In the sample table, add all the samples you prepared together with the corresponding Index read.c.In the sequencing software, click on sequencing. Follow the instructions on the sequencer, choose the new experiment created in the step above, and start the sequencer.Pause point: At this point, it is possible to store the samples at −20°C and continue the protocol at a later point.

steps.title: Prepare buffer stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required stock solutions as described, storing them under the conditions indicated in the buffer table.

substeps.instruction: MES buffer (500 mM, pH 5.3): dissolve 53.3 g MES monohydrate in 400 mL nuclease‑free ddH₂O, adjust pH to 5.3, then bring to 500 mL total volume.
polyU stock (41 mM monomer): dissolve 14.15 mg polyuridylic acid potassium salt in 1 mL nuclease‑free ddH₂O.

RG3 peptide stock (155 mM): dissolve 500 mg Ac‑FRGRGRGD in 1 mL nuclease‑free ddH₂O, adjust pH to 5.3 with ~475 µL 1 M NaOH, then add ddH₂O to a final volume of 2.475 mL. (Do not exceed this concentration; verify peptide purity by MS/HPLC.)
NaCl stock (5 M): dissolve 29.22 g NaCl in 70 mL nuclease‑free ddH₂O, then bring to 100 mL total volume.
EDC stock (400 mM): dissolve 19.2 mg EDC in 230 µL nuclease‑free ddH₂O. Prepare fresh; store at –20 °C under inert gas.
PEG‑8000 stock (50 % w/v): dissolve 20 g PEG‑8000 in 23 mL nuclease‑free ddH₂O, heat gently while stirring, then bring to 40 mL total volume. Do not exceed 40 mL.

steps.title: Assemble coacervate reaction
steps.instruction: Combine ssDNA library with all coacervate components, add fuel (EDC), incubate briefly, then separate phases by centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Thaw ssDNA library (and optional tagged RNA) on ice.
Prepare a 900 µL master mix with the following final concentrations (volumes in µL):
MES pH 5.3 500 mM – 200 µL
RG3 peptide 155 mM – 23 µL
polyU 41 mM – 4.1 µL
NaCl 5 M – 1 µL
ssDNA library 3 µg/µL – 9 µL (≈27 µg total)
Tagged RNA (optional) 100 µM – 1 µL (makes pellet easier to see).
Add 100 µL 400 mM EDC stock to the master mix and pipette up/down to mix. Turbidity should appear within seconds.
Incubate 1 min at ~25 °C (do not exceed 30 °C).
Centrifuge 3 min at 16 000 g, 25 °C (temperature must stay ≤30 °C).
Immediately remove all supernatant with a P1000 (bulk) followed by a P10 (residual) without disturbing the pellet; keep the supernatant for later analysis.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 µL 5 M NaCl by pipetting up/down, then add 40 µL ddH₂O (solution should become clear).

steps.title: Purify coacervate and supernatant DNA
steps.instruction: Use the Monarch Spin PCR & DNA Cleanup Kit (small‑oligo protocol) to clean both the pellet‑derived and supernatant‑derived DNA.

substeps.instruction: For each 50 µL of pellet solution and 50 µL of supernatant solution:
Add 100 µL Buffer BZ, then 300 µL isopropanol; mix by pipetting (no vortex).
Transfer the 450 µL mixture onto a spin column, spin 1 min at 16 000 g, discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µL Buffer WZ, spin 1 min at 16 000 g; discard flow‑through. Repeat this wash once more.
Place the column in a fresh 1.5 mL tube and spin empty for 1 min at 16 000 g to remove residual buffer.
Elute DNA by adding 10 µL ddH₂O to the matrix centre, spin 1 min at 16 000 g, and collect eluate.

steps.title: Digest polyU RNA
steps.instruction: Remove residual polyU RNA from both purified samples with RNase cocktail.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL RNase cocktail to each eluate (keep enzyme on a –20 °C block).
Incubate 2 h at 37 °C in a thermocycler, then 10 min at 65 °C with lid at 105 °C.
Optional: analyse 2 µL of the digested ssDNA on a 20 % 19:1 urea‑PAGE gel.

steps.title: Prepare splint‑ligated adapters
steps.instruction: Create P5 and P7 adapter‑splint mixes, anneal them, then ligate to the recovered ssDNA.

substeps.instruction: Thaw P5 and P7 adapter oligos and corresponding splints on ice.
For each sample, prepare 10 µL P5 mix:
10 µL 10× T4 DNA Ligase Reaction Buffer (1× final)
1 µL 100 µM SRSLY P5 adapter (10 µM final)
1 µL 100 µM SRSLY P5 splint (20 µM final)
2 µL ddH₂O.
Prepare 10 µL P7 mix analogously with P7 adapter and splint.
Anneal each 10 µL mix: heat to 95 °C for 10 s, then cool to 10 °C at 0.1 °C s⁻¹.
Prepare 78 µL ligation master mix per sample:
9 µL 10× T4 DNA Ligase Reaction Buffer (1× final)
9 µL P5 mix
9 µL P7 mix
9 µL ssDNA sample
2 µL ddH₂O.
Add 1 µL (30 U) T4 DNA Ligase and 1 µL (10 U) T4 PNK; mix gently.
Incubate ~16 h at 25 °C (lid off).
Heat 10 min at 65 °C (lid 105 °C) to inactivate enzymes.
Clean up 80 µL of ligation reaction with Monarch Spin PCR kit (standard protocol, 3:1 sample:binding‑buffer ratio):
Add 240 µL Buffer BZ, mix, transfer 320 µL onto column, spin 1 min at 16 000 g, discard flow‑through.
Add 200 µL Buffer WZ, spin 1 min at 16 000 g; repeat wash once.
Spin empty 1 min at 16 000 g, then elute with 17 µL ddH₂O.
Optional: run 2 µL of the cleaned product on a 20 % urea‑PAGE gel or TapeStation (expected length = library + 67 nt; e.g., N30 → 97 nt).
Pause point – store at –20 °C if needed.

steps.title: PCR amplify with index primers
steps.instruction: Add Illumina index and universal primers to the adapter‑ligated DNA and amplify.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 25 µL PCR mix per sample:
15 µL NEBNext Ultra II Q5 Master Mix (2×)
1 µL 5 µM index primer (NEB set)
5 µL 5 µM universal primer (NEB set)
4 µL adapter‑ligated DNA.
Run thermocycler:
98 °C 30 s (initial denaturation)
15 cycles of:
98 °C 10 s (denaturation)
65 °C 75 s (annealing/extension)
Final extension: 65 °C 300 s
Hold at 4 °C.
CRITICAL: Use a unique index primer for each sample.
Clean PCR product with NucleoMag NGS beads (size‑selection):
Resuspend beads, add 45 µL beads to each PCR, incubate 5 min.
Place on magnetic rack 5 min, discard supernatant.
Wash twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (30 s each), remove all liquid.
Air‑dry beads ≤5 min.
Elute with 33 µL 0.1 TE (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA), incubate 2 min.
Place on magnetic rack 5 min, transfer 30 µL eluate to a fresh tube.
Optional: verify library size on TapeStation (D1000 cassette).
Pause point – store at –20 °C if needed.

steps.title: Normalize and pool libraries for sequencing
steps.instruction: Dilute each library to 1 nM, pool equal volumes, add PhiX control, and prepare the final loading mix.

substeps.instruction: In low‑binding tubes, dilute each library to 1 nM with 10 mM Tris, pH 8.5.
Combine 10 µL of each 1 nM library into one tube (resulting in a 1 nM pooled library).
Prepare final loading library:
50 µL pooled 1 nM library → 5 pM final concentration
5 µL 1 nM PhiX Control → 50 pM final
5 µL 10 mM Tris pH 8.5 → bring to 10 mM final.
Mix gently; this is the loading library for the iSeq 100.

steps.title: Load iSeq 100 and run sequencing
steps.instruction: Prepare the iSeq 100 flow cell and cassette, load the library, and start the run with the specified settings.

substeps.instruction: Thaw the iSeq flow cell 30 min at ~25 °C.
Unpack the sequencing cassette, invert it 5×, tap 5× on the bench.
Pierce the foil over the library loading well with a pipette tip.
Load 20 µL of the final loading library into the well.
Insert the flow cell into the cassette, then insert the cassette into the iSeq 100.
In Local Run Manager set up a new run:
Method: “Generate FastQ”
Experiment name: (choose)
Library prep protocol: “Custom”
Index read: 1 (P7) – 6 bp
Read mode: dual‑read, 151 bp each.
Add all samples with their corresponding index reads in the sample table.
Start the sequencing run.

steps.title: Illumina SAV quality control
steps.instruction: Inspect raw sequencing run metrics using Illumina Sequencing Analysis Viewer.

substeps.instruction: Copy the entire results folder to a computer with SAV installed.
Open SAV, browse to the folder, and open it.
On the Analysis screen review quality statistics per cycle.
Switch to Imaging → Scatter Plot, plot “% Occupied” (x‑axis) vs “% Pass Filter” (y‑axis).
Interpretation: oval cloud = good loading; diagonal line (x≈y) = underloaded; vertical band at 95‑100 % Occupied = overloaded.

steps.title: FastQC and MultiQC of FASTQ files
steps.instruction: Run FastQC on raw FASTQ files and aggregate reports with MultiQC.

substeps.instruction: If needed, gunzip *.fastq.gz (bash: gunzip *.fastq.gz).
Create a conda environment: `conda create -n fastqc-env fastqc multiqc -c bioconda -c conda-forge`.
Activate: `conda activate fastqc-env`.
Run FastQC on all FASTQ files: `fastqc *.fastq`.
Run MultiQC in the same directory: `multiqc .`.

steps.title: Adapter trimming with cutadapt
steps.instruction: Trim Illumina adapters from paired‑end reads using cutadapt for each sample.

substeps.instruction: Create a conda environment: `conda create -n cutadapt-env cutadapt -c bioconda -c conda-forge`.
For variables Ref, Sup, Pel run:
Activate env, then:
cutadapt -a "AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCA" -A "AGATCGGAAGAGCGTCGTGTAGGGAAAGAGTGT" --discard-untrimmed -o ${var}_trim_1.fastq -p ${var}_trim_2.fastq ${var}_R1.fastq ${var}_R2.fastq
Deactivate env, activate fastqc‑env, run FastQC on trimmed files, then deactivate.
Confirm successful trimming by inspecting FastQC reports.

steps.title: Length filtering with seqkit
steps.instruction: Keep only reads exactly 30 nt long (the library length).

substeps.instruction: Create env: `conda create -n seqkit-env seqkit -c bioconda -c conda-forge`.
For each variable (Ref, Sup, Pel):
Activate env, run:
seqkit seq -m 30 -M 30 ${var}_trim_1.fastq > ${var}_fil_1.fastq
seqkit seq -m 30 -M 30 ${var}_trim_2.fastq > ${var}_fil_2.fastq
Deactivate env, run FastQC on the filtered files (fastqc‑env).

steps.title: Convert FASTQ to FASTA (R1 only)
steps.instruction: Generate FASTA files from the filtered R1 FASTQ files for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Run: `seqkit fq2fa Ref_fil_1.fastq -o Ref_fil_1.fasta` (repeat for Sup and Pel).

steps.title: Calculate nucleotide composition per position
steps.instruction: Use Python (pandas, numpy, matplotlib) to compute base percentages at each position of the 30‑nt reads.

substeps.instruction: Install packages: `conda install pandas matplotlib -c conda-forge`.
Run the provided Python script that reads each FASTA, builds a DataFrame, counts nucleotides per position, converts to percentages, and stores results in `df_perc`.

steps.title: Plot nucleotide composition
steps.instruction: Generate per‑sample line plots of base percentages across the 30 positions.

substeps.instruction: Use the supplied Python script (matplotlib) which sets font to Arial, size 9, weight bold, creates a 2.5 × 2 in figure, plots G (orange), A (red), C (blue), T (green), adds grid, titles, labels, y‑ticks (15‑40 % step 5), saves as `<variant>_content.pdf` and shows the plot.

steps.title: Calculate and plot differences vs reference
steps.instruction: Subtract the reference nucleotide percentages from each sample and plot the delta.

substeps.instruction: Create `df_diff` = `df_perc[variant]` – `df_perc[Ref]` for each variant.
Plot G, A, C, T lines (same colors) with y‑ticks –8 to 8 % step 4, save as `<variant>_difference.pdf`.

steps.title: Predict minimum‑free‑energy structures with RNAfold
steps.instruction: Run RNAfold (DNA parameters) on each FASTA and extract dot‑bracket structures and ΔG values.

substeps.instruction: Install ViennaRNA package per vendor instructions.
Create a file `file_list.txt` containing paths to Ref, Sup, Pel FASTA files.
Run the bash loop (see protocol) which for each file:
`RNAfold -i $input_fasta --noPS --noconv -P DNA > $rnafold_output`
Extract lines containing '(' into `${filename}_deltaG.txt`.
Parse the first 30 characters as dot‑bracket, characters 31‑ onward as ΔG (numeric).
Write dot‑bracket to `${filename}_dot_bracket.txt` and ΔG to `${filename}_energy.txt`.

steps.title: Analyse ΔG distributions
steps.instruction: Bin ΔG values (10 bins from –10 to 0 kcal mol⁻¹) and plot frequency curves.

substeps.instruction: Load each `${variant}_fil_1_energy.txt` into pandas.
Bin using `np.digitize` with edges `np.linspace(-10,0,11)`.
Compute frequency per bin (counts / total reads).
Plot all three variants on one figure (2.5 × 2.5 in), label axes, legend, save as `deltaG.pdf`.

steps.title: Report average ΔG per sample
steps.instruction: Calculate mean ΔG for Ref, Sup, and Pel.

substeps.instruction: For each variant, compute `df[variant]['values'].mean()` and print (rounded to 3 dp).

steps.title: Discover enriched motifs with STREME
steps.instruction: Run MEME‑suite STREME (RNA mode) to find motifs enriched in a sample versus the reference.

substeps.instruction: Install MEME‑suite per website instructions.
Execute:
`streme –p ../len_fil/pel_fil_1.fasta –n ../len_fil/sup_fil_1.fasta –o streme_output –maxw 10 --rna`
Extract motif definitions from `streme_output/streme.txt` (lines beginning with “MOTIF”).

steps.title: Plot motif logos and positional statistics
steps.instruction: Convert STREME output to logo matrices, compute information content, and generate multi‑panel figures.

substeps.instruction: Parse `motifs.txt` and `sites.tsv` with the provided Python scripts (regex, defaultdict).
Calculate information content per position (`ic = log2(4) + Σ p*log2(p)`).
Create data structures for positional hit counts, start and end site frequencies.
Generate per‑motif plots: information‑content logo, nucleotide‑content logo, positional hit line, start‑site line, end‑site line (using logomaker and matplotlib).
Assemble all motifs into a combined figure with 5 columns per motif; save as `combined_motifs_all_in_one.pdf`.

steps.title: Compute abstracted structures with RNAshapes
steps.instruction: Run RNAshapes on each FASTA to obtain abstracted secondary‑structure representations.

substeps.instruction: Create conda env: `conda create -n RNAshapes-env RNAshapes -c bioconda`.
For each variable (Ref, Sup, Pel) run: `RNAshapes -c 0 <${var}_fil_1.fasta> ${var}_abstract.txt`.
Parse each `${var}_abstract.txt` to extract Energy, DotBracket, and Abstracted columns (Python script).

steps.title: Analyse abstracted structure frequencies
steps.instruction: Count occurrences of each abstracted structure and plot normalized percentages.

substeps.instruction: For each variable, compute `df['Abstracted'].value_counts()` and store as a DataFrame with columns `Structure` and `Occurrences`.
Create a combined bar plot (log‑scale y) showing percentage of sequences for each structure across Ref, Sup, Pel (Python script).
Save as `Abstracted_Structures.pdf`.

steps.title: Stem‑length analysis
steps.instruction: Determine stem lengths from dot‑bracket notation, compute distributions, and plot density curves.

substeps.instruction: Add a column `StemLength` = count of '(' in each `DotBracket` (Python).
Count occurrences of each stem length per variant, store as DataFrames.
Determine maximum stem length across all variants.
Plot normalized stem‑length density for each variant (different colors), fill under curves, set x‑ticks every 2 units, save as `StemLength_Density.pdf`.
